content:
maya: apac cluster svc-apac-2a is seeing large request queues and token latency spiking to 2s per token. Dashboard shows batcher backlog + KV cache eviction storms. :warning:
alex: seeing it too, allocator is repeatedly failing to bind GPUs on new pods. logs show `manifest_index: checksum mismatch` during scheduler sync.
sam: confirmed packet loss between apac-control and apac-edge-2a earlier, could be a control-plane partition. routing is still sending traffic there.
maya: marking as incident, hitting paging. Can infra team pause routing to apac-2a and divert to apac-2b / na1 fallback? :eyes:
alex: starting: scale up hotpool in apac-2b and enable fallback routing. running commands now:
```sh
# scale reserved pool
kubectl -n infra scale deploy/hotpool-apac-2b --replicas=6
# set routing override to prefer apac-2b
redwoodctl routing set-priority --region apac-2b --weight 80
```
li: hold on scaling — burst will cost a lot. what's current spend vs SLA?
natalie: we have emergency budget for failover. prefer minimizing customer impact. proceed but keep tracking spend.
infra-bot: [deploy] scheduler-patch v2026.03.18-prelim applied to apac-control-1 (CI#3421) :rocket:
alex: patch added defensive check for manifest index and will refuse to schedule pods until index rebuild. that prevented further bad allocations but left capacity low -> queues grew -> runtime batcher started misbehaving and triggered KV cache thrash.
sam: runtime team, can you temporarily disable continuous batching for requests routed to apac-2a to reduce queuing?
li: patch command to toggle batching affinity:
```json
{"region":"apac-2a","continuous_batching":false}
```
maya: runtime team acknowledged. disabling now.

alex: also initiated manifest index repair on apac-control-1: `repair_index --source s3://manifests/apac/ --force` — it's 60% synced. expect 8-12m.

sam: traffic reroute to apac-2b is in effect, latency for affected customers is dropping. KV eviction rates down ~70%.

natalie: please post brief customer-facing blurb after we have stable numbers. ops to draft.

li: cost note: scaling hotpool + burst instances will add ~12% to monthly committed for this region if sustained. I'll open a ticket to auto-reclaim once healthy.

maya: current mitigation list:
- routing override to apac-2b/na1: done
- disable continuous batching on apac-2a: done
- manifest index repair in progress: running
- scheduler patch deployed to apac-control-1: done (prelim)
- hotpool scaled in apac-2b: done
- monitor KV eviction + batcher backlog: ongoing

alex: logs showing residual error: `kvcache: eviction loop exceeded threshold, throttling enabled` — reducing per-request token window as temporary stopgap.
sam: can we enable prefix cache warmup on apac-2b to reduce cold misses?

maya: yes, enabling warmup. command:
`redis-cli -h apac-2b-kv warmup-prefixes /etc/redwood/warmup-list.txt`

infra-bot: alert cleared for `control-plane-partition` once manifest sync completed. incident mode: monitoring.

natalie: great work. action items: alex follow up on root cause of manifest checksum flip; li ensure cost reclaim automation; runtime team write postmortem outline with latency graphs. will draft customer note once we confirm stable for 30m. :thumbsup:

maya: will keep thread updated. thanks all.
